To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the multinomial model provides a more accurate description of the scRNA Seq data than the Poisson model and that the multinomial based methods provide better clustering results than the Poisson based methods.
we propose simple multinomial methods that outperform current practice for scRNA Seq analysis.

1) the UMI counts follow a multinomial distribution; 2) the current normalization procedures, such as log of count per million and highly variable genes selection, produce false variability in the dimension reduction; 3) the multinomial based dimension reduction and feature selection methods outperform current practices in downstream clustering assessment using real datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of scRNA Seq data.
the analysis of high dimensional data sets with many missing values.
the problem of feature selection and dimension reduction for single cell RNA Seq data, using a multinomial model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is superior to current practice in the field of scRNA Seq data analysis.
the use of UMI counts and the proposed multinomial based methods are superior to current practice.
we have proposed simple multinomial methods for feature selection and dimension reduction in single cell RNA Seq data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multinomial distribution is the appropriate statistical model for UMI counts, and that the GLM is a powerful tool for feature selection in single cell data.
we have proposed a multinomial model for single cell data and used this model to propose a new feature selection method and a new method to reduce dimensionality.
we propose a new method of normalization and feature selection for scRNA Seq data based on a multinomial model that outperforms current methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multinomial model is a good approximation for the UMI data, and that the multinomial GLM PCA and feature selection methods are useful for downstream analysis.
the UMI counts from scRNA Seq follow a multinomial sampling distribution, which is not the case for bulk RNA Seq data.
current normalization and feature selection procedures for scRNA Seq data are not optimal and that simple, alternative approaches exist.
